items.title: Lew Soloff interviewed by Monk Rowe, Scottsdale, Arizona, April 16, 2000
items.q: Actually so was Al Cooper, before I was there. I loved his songs.

ctx.x: Yeah, he had less arrangements on those records than he should have.

Near the end, yeah. Of course. Because he didn’t want to bring something in and have it put down. And he was the real, amazing creative energy in that band. Actually so was Al Cooper, before I was there. I loved his songs. But it doesn’t matter. I’m always of the mind that if a band is allowed to just continuously try to be creative they’re better off than if they have a hit and they try to keep following that formula. I’m even of that mind with the Manhattan Jazz Quintet which I’m in, which you may have heard of…
